title: Bench & Boarding — quick capture (Applied ML weekly notes)
content:
TL;DR: Quick weekly capture from 10/18 standups + bench session. Focus this week: compact quant experiments for MPT-style 7B variant onboarding, KV-cache interactions with 4-bit GPQ, and a lightweight eval pass for hallucination regressions. Lots of small wins; still noisy in long-seq latency numbers

Attendees (10/18): Asha, Ethan, Maya, Liam, Joon (infra consult), Claire (SRE check-in)

Notes / highlights:
- Model onboarding: started with mpt-7b-chat-lite (fp16 baseline). Goal: onboard a 4-bit quantized variant that keeps <=2% ppl delta on evaluation prompts while cutting memory ~2.6x.
  - Approach: two-prong: 1) Symmetric 4-bit with per-channel scale (baseline quant packer prototype); 2) GPTQ-derived 4-bit (post-training int8->4 conversion) tested via local conversion script.
  - Early result (small eval set, 120 prompts, mixed length):
    - fp16 baseline: mean token latency 43ms (seq=256, batch=1), mem 12.1GB
    - symmetric 4-bit: mean token latency 37ms, mem 4.6GB, ppl delta +1.8%
    - GPTQ-4-bit: mean token latency 35ms, mem 4.1GB, ppl delta +2.7% (higher variance on named-entity prompts)
  - Action: run a 1k-prompt head-to-head with full eval suite and longer-context (seq=1024) by EOD Fri (Ethan). Log attached PR#782 has conversion scripts and golden-run flags.

- KV-cache stress observation:
  - When using 4-bit GPTQ variant, KV-cache fill rate drops slightly (we suspect rounding/pack padding causing extra memcpy). Measured: throughput drop ~3-6% at seq>512 under continuous-batching.
  - Hypothesis: our pack/unpack path uses a 64-byte aligned temporary buffer in the runtime; GPTQ quant layout induces extra unpack ops.
  - Experiment: Maya to run patch that preallocates aligned buffer and bypasses memcpy for simple-copy paths. Also run microbenchmark (kvfill-64k) to capture difference.

- Eval / quality gating:
  - Ran targeted hallucination evals (policy/regression set of 420 prompts) against both quant variants. Observations:
    - Symmetric 4-bit showed fewer hallucinations on ref-trace tasks (maybe smoothing from per-channel scales).
    - GPTQ-4-bit had occasional deterministic hallucination on temporal ranking tasks (3 cases reproducible).
  - Decided to add the hallucination metric as a gating check in onboarding pipeline: if hallucination delta > 1.5% vs baseline, fail auto-onboard.

- Microbench results snapshot (run id: bench-20261018-A):

  model_variant | seq | batch | mean_token_ms | mem_GB | ppl_delta
  ---------------|-----|-------|---------------|--------|---------
  fp16_baseline   | 256 | 1     | 43            | 12.1   | 0.0%
  sym_4bit_pack   | 256 | 1     | 37            | 4.6    | +1.8%
  gptq_4bit_conv  | 256 | 1     | 35            | 4.1    | +2.7%

- CI / automation notes:
  - Onboarding pipeline needs small change: add a step to run the KV-cache microbench for seq buckets (256, 512, 1024) and capture jitter-percentiles (p50/p95/p99).
  - Maya opened a PR for adding jitter capture framework (small wrapper around perf-runner). Waiting on infra creds review (Joon).

- Standup quick decisions:
  - Do not auto-promote GPTQ-4bit until 1k-prompt eval completes and KV-cache microbench is green.
  - Symmetric 4-bit qualifies for canary if hallucination gating passes on larger eval. Canary release plan: 50 qps on dedicated pool, 24h, rollback if error rate or hallucination metric regresses by >1%.

Risks / unknowns:
- Memory accounting mismatch in dedicated nodes when quant variant is loaded with prepacked weights -> reported host mem lower than actual (we saw OOM on dedicated-staging-3 once). Need closer inspection of allocator accounting (SRE/infra to assist).
- Long-tail latency under continuous-batching still noisy for seq>1024; may need to adjust batching window heuristics for quant variants.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Ethan: run 1k-prompt full eval for both quant variants, produce per-task ppl/precision/recall, upload results to Confluence. ETA: 2026-10-21
- Maya: implement aligned-buffer bypass patch + kv microbench run (bench-20261019-B). ETA: 2026-10-19
- Liam: add hallucination metric to onboarding gate and wire to console alerting. ETA: 2026-10-22
- Joon: review infra creds and confirm canary pool allocation for 50 qps. ETA: 2026-10-20
- Asha (me): collate notes and produce short summary for next product sync (note: include gating thresholds and suggested rollback policy). ETA: 2026-10-23

Loose thoughts / threads to follow:
- Would a mixed-precision approach (kv-cache in float16, attn/ffn 4-bit) give better latency/mem tradeoff? Quick sims suggest memory ~6.3GB with ppls ~+1.2% — worth a micro-PoC.
- Consider adding a small randomized prompt set to onboarding (10% of eval) specifically designed to surface temporal hallucinations; current deterministic suite misses some reproducible failures.

Meeting transcript snippets (raw):
  Asha: "we're seeing 3-6% throughput drop when seq>512, that's consistent across two runs"
  Maya: "I think packer is forcing extra copies for non-aligned shapes — I'll try aligned buffers"
  Ethan: "if 4-bit gets us sub-5ms token savings we can open dedicated canaries sooner, but quality gating is the hard part"

Files / artifacts to attach:
- bench logs: s3://redwood-bench/bench-20261018-A/logs.tar.gz (attached on PR 782)
- conversion scripts: github PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-inference/pull/782
- short slide: confluence page https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/compact-quant-playbook

Open questions for product sync:
- Acceptable hallucination delta for canary? proposed <=1.5% vs baseline.
- Canary sizing: 50 qps seems safe but does it buy enough signal for hallucination metric? maybe need longer duration if metric is noisy.

Next sync: quick check-in Friday 10/22 11:00am — bring 1k-eval partial results and kv microbench numbers.

Notes-to-self: keep a clean artifact chain (bench id, seed, commit SHA). If a variant is promoted to dedicated, tag release with gating report.

Random small TODO (scratch):
- Add unit test for packer alignment edge cases (Maya)
- Add a tiny histogram view in console for hallucination event types (Liam)
- Run memory accounting job across dedicated-staging nodes to reproduce OOM (Joon)

End of quick capture. Will expand into a formal onboarding doc if results are stable.
